newsitem.title: INDIA: India L&T to invest 10 bln rupees yearly in growth.
newsitem.headline: India L&T to invest 10 bln rupees yearly in growth.

text.p: India's largest engineering and construction firm, Larsen & Toubro Ltd (L&T) said on Tuesday it plans to spend between 10 billion and 12 billion rupees annually to finance growth and expansion plans.
"I think our annual capital expenditure would be of the order of 10 billion rupees to 12 billion rupees," L&T managing director Sudhakar Kulkarni told Reuters in an interview.
A large portion would be used to fund L&T's expansion of its cement capacity to more than 12 million tonnes from its present figure of 6.5 million tonnes by the turn of the century, Kulkarni added.
L&T is India's second largest cement maker. The firm recently announced a net profit of 4.11 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, up from 3.89 billion in the previous year.
L&T plans to double the capacity of its plant in the western state of Gujarat to four million tonnes.
A second plant in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, with a two million tonne capacity is nearing completion early in the first quarter of 1998/99 (April-March).
"Then we plan to double the capacity of that plant later on by the year 2000/2001, so we will have a total capacity of 12 million tonnes by the turn of the century," Kulkarni added.
Another component of the expenditure would be made up of investments in captive power plants to insulate the cement plants from local power outages.

"If we have these capacities we don't want to be dependent on the grid," Kulkarni said. "We want to be on our own so far as power is concerned so that we get power adequately, also the quality required, voltage, frequencies and so on."
"So we have decided to put up our own power plants. We are working today on two power plants, one is for our Gujarat cement plant and one is for our Awarpur cement plant (in Maharashtra)," he said.
The capital expenditure plan also envisaged substantial investments in infrastructure projects that L&T is building on a Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) basis, Kulkarni added.

"There are three projects basically - the Narmada bridge (in central India), the Coimbatore bypass (southern India), and a captive power plant for Haldia Petrochemicals (eastern India)," Kulkarni said.

L&T has set up the Narmada Infrastructure Construction Co Ltd to execute a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) order for the construction of a 1.32 km bridge across the Narmada river, with a 300-million rupee investment in its equity.

Another new company, HPL Cogeneration Ltd, will build a combined cycle power cogeneration plant for the Haldia Petrochemicals Co Ltd, with L&T subscribing 866 million rupees of the firm's 1.17 billion rupee equity.
The plant will be built on a Build-Own-Operate basis.
"...I think this is what we have really tied up in the last six months, and we expect every year a few such projects, so that will require some investments also."
In its annual report released on Monday, L&T said it planned to make investments upto two billion rupees in special purpose vehicle companies to take up BOT/BOOT projects.

"The company is also exploring proposals with good prospects and or synergy with the business of the company," it added. "The requirement of investment in such companies is estimated at two billion rupees," it added.
